2013). A biomarker of choline status should clearly track with dose-response changes in choline intake and be strongly associated
with health and disease. Plasma choline and its metabolites are frequently measured as markers of choline status, typically by liquid
chromatography/electrospray ionization, stable isotope dilution (tandem) mass spectrometry, though other methods to measure
choline, such as colorimetric kits, are available. Fasting plasma choline levels do not always track with moderate changes in choline
intake (Veenema et al., 2008; Abratte et al., 2009), and rarely drop below 4.5 mM in individuals consuming deﬁcient diets; neverthe-
less, fasting plasma choline levels, particularly in repleted individuals previously consuming low intakes and in those consuming
high supplemental intakes, can be responsive to choline intakes. Plasma choline levels should be considered as not only an
